summary: A linked list starts and ends with 0 and has 0-separated segments; replace each segment by one node holding its sum and drop all zeros.
mainInsight: Walk the list once. Reuse the first node of each segment to hold the segment's sum, then link it straight to the first node of the next segment, skipping the zero in between. No new nodes, O(1) extra space.
invariant: Every node before `modify` already holds the sum of one finished segment, and they are linked in order.
canonicalApproach: In-place merge reusing the first node of each segment

approaches.name: Build a new list
approaches.summary: Sum each segment and append a new node to a dummy-headed result list.
strengths: Simple, does not touch the input

approaches.name: In-place merge reusing the first node of each segment
approaches.summary: Write each sum into the segment's first node and relink past the zero.

personalSolution.approach: In-place merge: the first node of each segment receives the sum and links to the next segment
personalSolution.notes: Optimal. Starting with dummy = head means the first round writes 0 into the leading zero node, which is why you return head.next; starting from head.next makes that clearer.

canonicalCode:
class Solution:
    def mergeNodes(self, head: 'ListNode | None') -> 'ListNode | None':
        modify = head.next            # first node of the current segment will hold its sum
        scan = head.next
        while scan:                   # every node is visited once: O(n)
            total = 0
            while scan.val != 0:      # sum the segment up to the next zero
                total += scan.val
                scan = scan.next
            modify.val = total
            scan = scan.next          # step past the zero
            modify.next = scan        # link to the next segment (None after the last zero)
            modify = scan
        return head.next
commonMistakes: Leaving the trailing zero in the result.
Returning head (a zero node) instead of head.next.
Creating a node for an empty segment (impossible here: no two consecutive zeros).
edgeCases: Nodes with value 0 only at the separators (guaranteed).

cards.answer: cur starts at the leading zero, so the inner loop does not run: total = 0 is written back into head, cur moves to the first data node, head.next is set to it, and dummy moves there. From then on each segment's first node receives its sum. head is just a 0 placeholder, so the answer starts at head.next.
keyPoints: Inner loop skipped at the leading zero
Later rounds write sums into each segment's first node
